Now, offers at $40B+

AI chip startup Etched is reportedly fielding investment offers at $40 billion or more, with some bids as high as $50 billion — just weeks after raising $700 million at a $21 billion valuation, a round led by Jane Street.

What makes Etched different? Instead of building general-purpose GPUs like Nvidia, it built Sohu — a chip designed to run only one thing: transformer models, the architecture behind today's AI.

The company has disclosed around $1 billion in booked customer contracts.

It's a big bet: if transformers stay at the heart of AI, specialized chips could beat general-purpose GPUs on inference cost and speed.

7513543651239862275.author: Maya Levinson
7513543651239862275.text: Etched's reported valuation offers have arrived only a couple of months after a $700 million round valued it at $21 billion. The company is building entire AI systems around proprietary inference chips, so the capital requirement is closer to industrial infrastructure than a typical software startup. Smaller AI businesses benefit when hardware competition eventually pushes inference prices down, even though they cannot participate in the chip race directly. The question is how much of today's valuation assumes those lower costs arrive before the hardware has been proven at scale.

63% of an AI chip's parts bill is memory.

That's Epoch AI's estimate for late 2025, and the memory in question is HBM.

HBM is a stack of memory chips placed right next to the processor. It feeds the processor data fast enough to keep it busy. Without it, the most powerful AI chip sits waiting.

And the price of HBM is about to jump.

WHAT'S CHANGING

Samsung is reportedly asking more than 3x the current price for next year's HBM4 (Maeil Business). TrendForce expects average HBM prices to rise 121% in 2027. UBS says about 79%.

The reason is physics. Micron says HBM uses about 3x the silicon of regular memory for the same capacity. 

So every HBM chip made means fewer of
everything else.
